S1.title: Python Exercise Guide
S1.text:
Exercise Set A: Variables and Control Flow
Exercise A1. Write a program that asks for a temperature in Celsius and prints it in Fahrenheit. The formula is F = C * 9 / 5 + 32. Expected result: 100 Celsius becomes 212.0 Fahrenheit.
Exercise A2. Print all even numbers from 1 to 20 using a for loop and the modulo operator. Hint: a number n is even when n % 2 == 0. A common mistake is writing range(1, 20), which stops at 19; use range(1, 21).
Exercise A3. Implement FizzBuzz for numbers 1 to 30. Print "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for multiples of 5 and "FizzBuzz" for multiples of both. The test for multiples of both must come first, otherwise the Fizz branch will catch the number 15 too early.

S2.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S2.text: affects 1% of people; a test detects it 95% of the time (sensitivity) and gives a false positive 5% of the time.  P(positive) = 0.95 * 0.01 + 0.05 * 0.99 = 0.059. So P(disease | positive) = 0.0095 / 0.059, about 0.161. Even after a positive test, the probability of disease is only about 16% because the disease is rare. This is the base rate effect.

S5.title: Python Lecture Notes
S5.text: count from the end, so "python"[-1] is "n". Slicing "python"[1:4] returns "yth" (start included, stop excluded).  F-strings embed expressions inside text: f"Total: {price * 2:.2f}" formats a number with two decimals. Integer division // discards the fractional part (7 // 2 is 3), the modulo operator % returns the remainder (7 % 2 is 1), and ** is exponentiation (2 ** 10 is 1024). Dividing with / always returns a float, so 6 / 3 is 2.0.
